source.title: ADOPT: Modified Adam Can Converge with Any β2 with the Optimal Rate
source.authors: Shohei Taniguchi; Keno Harada; Gouki Minegishi; Yuta Oshima; Seonghyun Jeong; Go Nagahara; Tomoshi Iiyama; Masahiro Suzuki; Yusuke Iwasawa; Yutaka Matsuo

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares ADOPT with other adaptive optimizers on held-out performance, but does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD, as V4 requires.
record.gate_note: The paper reports held-out results for adaptive-optimizer comparisons. These do not establish whether adaptive methods perform worse than SGD, so they are recorded as findings that fit no version. Theoretical convergence analysis and cited prior-work results are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares ADOPT with other adaptive optimizers and analyzes optimization convergence. It reports no adaptive-versus-SGD held-out comparison for V4. Its GPT-2 batch-size experiment does not establish a fixed epoch budget or isolate a large-batch generalization penalty required by V5. None of its results tests another listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that ADOPT addresses Adam's convergence problem and improves performance across their tested applications. The theoretical guarantee assumes smoothness, unbiased stochastic gradients and uniformly bounded gradient second moments; Appendix B gives a counterexample under sampling without replacement.
record.recipe_differences: The paper proposes ADOPT, changing the second-moment estimate and the order of momentum update and normalization. Its empirical optimizer comparisons use adaptive methods and do not reproduce the adaptive-versus-SGD comparisons in V4.
record.method_sensitivity: The GPT-2 comparison reports a batch-size-dependent difference: Adam has loss spikes at batch size 96, while both methods work well at batch size 480. Exact validation-loss values are shown only in Figure 5.

fits_no_version.finding: ADOPT performs slightly better in the reported MNIST and CIFAR-10 classifier experiments and achieves higher ImageNet accuracy than AdamW and AMSGrad.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ADOPT improves classifier performance over the tested adaptive-optimizer baselines in these settings.

fits_no_version.finding: NVAE test negative log-likelihood is lower with ADOPT than Adamax at both reported training durations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ADOPT improves MNIST density-estimation likelihood relative to Adamax under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-2 training with Adam becomes unstable at batch size 96; ADOPT trains stably. Both work at batch size 480, with ADOPT described as slightly better.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested GPT-2 recipe exhibits optimizer-dependent sensitivity to batch size and gradient noise.

fits_no_version.finding: Instruction-finetuned LLaMA-7B scores 42.13 on MMLU with ADOPT versus 41.2 with the baseline optimizer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ADOPT improves aggregate MMLU performance under this instruction-finetuning recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors report slightly improved continuous-control performance with ADOPT versus Adam.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ADOPT slightly improves soft actor-critic performance in the reported control experiment.

record.problems: Most held-out accuracy and loss comparisons are figure-only in the supplied text, so exact values cannot be extracted. Several experiments compare only adaptive optimizers; the paper does not test the SGD comparison central to V4. The text reports three trials for MNIST and the reinforcement-learning figure, and reports confidence intervals for ImageNet and MNIST NVAE results.
record.rows_left_out: No separately quantified SGD comparison is reported. The MNIST classifier, CIFAR-10, GPT-2, and reinforcement-learning plots are included as figure-only rows because the text provides qualitative descriptions but no exact values. No other optimizer comparisons with held-out outcomes are omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and training recipe.
Held-out error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, including recovery through weight decay or optimizer switching.

Large-versus-small-batch held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove any penalty. GPT-2 batch sizes 96 and 480 are examined, but the required budget control is not established.
Held-out effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of generalization gaps and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claims, even where numerical method-performance differences are clear. Missing numerical plot values do not themselves establish absence of an effect. Optimization convergence guarantees are distinct from held-out generalization.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD or momentum SGD; no such comparison is reported.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets.
Effects of dropout on held-out error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the generalization gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.
